data.why: The repository ships its own FoLiA-annotated test document (testflat.folia.xml, Dutch text with POS, lemma, morphology, chunking, entity, dependency and a spelling correction already encoded) used by FLAT's own interface test suite, which exercises every annotation type the editor supports.

goals: Upload a FoLiA document and view its token and span annotations (POS, lemma, morphology, chunking, dependencies)
Set an annotation focus (e.g. dependency or entity) to get a global colour-coded overview of that annotation type across the document
Correct an existing annotation (e.g. the pre-encoded spelling correction 'zei'->'zij') and verify the original is preserved as a correction, not overwritten
Add a new annotation to a word that doesn't yet have one, recording annotator and confidence
Edit document-wide metadata using the Metadata Editor mode
Use the undo/version history (git-backed) to revert an annotation change

review.summary: The tree captures FLAT's main purpose well: view a FoLiA document with one annotation layer in focus, inspect each word by hovering, correct or add annotations with confidence, and verify that provenance and originals are kept in the XML. I opened 12 cited screens and every one supports its node. It needs small fixes before filing: t11's wording, one missing screen citation, the uncovered menus for choosing which annotation types are shown, and some trimming of overlap between features; search, alternatives, tree views and undo remain gaps because they were not reached.
